title: Amounts and speed over time
question: How have the number of permits, the value and homes permitted, and the wait moved since 2012, and is the business concentrating in fewer firms?
finding: The City issued 37,290 building permits in 2019 and 22,872 in 2025; construction value permitted peaked at $5.4 billion in 2017 and was $2.7 billion in 2025; net new homes on issued permits went from 4,899 in 2019 to 2,216 in 2025. A full-review alteration issued in 2019 had waited a median 292 days, in 2023 328, in 2025 173. The ten largest contractors were named on permits carrying 31% of permitted value in 2012 to 2014 and 32% in 2023 to 2025, and on 5.2% and 8.5% of permits by number. By value the share swings with a few very large projects and shows no trend; by number of permits the ten largest contractors' share rose, most of the change coming in 2020 when the number of permits issued fell by 47%.
how: All building permits by year of issue, 2012 to 2026 (the file holds applications filed from 2012, so the first years miss permits filed earlier and issued then). Value is the department's revised cost where given, else the applicant's estimate. Homes are the homes in new buildings plus homes added by alterations to buildings that already had homes, on issued permits. Median days run from filing to issue. The concentration columns take, for each year, the ten firms named on the most permitted value in each role and divide by all value permitted that year; the last column does the same by number of permits for contractors.
limits: Declared cost is the applicant's own figure, and one permit can dominate a year: the largest single permit was 14% of all value permitted in 2017. The value shares therefore jump with the project cycle and are not a trend by themselves. A permit can name more than one firm in a role. Years before 2014 are thin because applications filed before 2012 are not in the file. Homes on issued permits are not homes built. 2026 runs to November 10.
